FIRST AMENDMENT TO ON-CALL GENERAL SERVICE AGREEMENT
This First Amendment (“First Amendment”) to the On-Call General Services Agreement
(“Agreement”) is made and entered into in the County of Ventura, State of California, this
______ day of __________, 20___, by and between the City of Oxnard, a municipal corporation
(“City”), and Collicutt Energy Services, Inc. (“Service Provider”). This First Amendment
amends the Agreement entered into on August 1, 2025, by City and Service Provider.
City and Service Provider agree as follows:
WHEREAS, the City of Oxnard owns and operates the Water Resource Recovery
Facility (WRRF), a 31.7 million gallon per day treatment plant that includes anaerobic digestion
and a cogeneration system essential for providing electricity and heat to support wastewater
treatment processes;
WHEREAS, the WRRF’s cogeneration facility, originally constructed in 1975, utilizes
three engine-driven generators, and Engine No. 3 permanently failed in summer 2024, requiring
the facility to rely solely on Engines No. 1 and No. 2 for heat production and supplemental
electricity;
WHEREAS, the remaining cogeneration engines are aging, increasingly worn, and
operating under heightened stress due to the loss of Engine No. 3, resulting in more frequent
breakdowns and an elevated need for specialized generator maintenance services;
WHEREAS, the City executed Agreement No. 32600082 with Collicutt Energy
Services, Inc. for on-call generator maintenance and minor repair services for the WRRF, but the
increased operational demands on Engines No. 1 and No. 2 have resulted in service needs that
exceed the funding levels contemplated in the Original Agreement;
WHEREAS, the parties mutually desire to amend the Original Agreement to increase the
not to exceed value, and authorize additional generator maintenance services necessary to ensure
continued safe and reliable WRRF operations through the existing agreement term;
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set
forth herein, the parties agree to amend the Original Agreement as set forth in the Amendment.
1. The “Not to Exceed Amount” in Section 5 of the Agreement is hereby amended to
“$495,000.00”
2. As so amended, the Agreement remains in full force and effect.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA REPORT
INFORMATION/CONSENT AGENDA
AGENDA ITEM NO. L.7
DATE: January 20, 2026
TO: City Council
FROM: Michael Wolfe, Public Works Director, (805) 385-8055, michael.wolfe@oxnard.org
SUBJECT: First Amendment to On-Call General Services Agreement 32600082 with Collicutt Energy Services, Inc.
for Generator Maintenance Services for the Wastewater Division.
RECOMMENDATION
That the City Council approve and authorize the execution of a First Amendment to an On-Call General Services
Agreement with Collicutt Energy Services, Inc. (Collicutt) to increase the not-to-exceed amount from $220,000 to
$495,000, for additional generator maintenance services for the Wastewater Division.
(This item did not originate in Committee.)
BACKGROUND
The City of Oxnard owns and operates the Water Resource Recovery Facility (WRRF) located at 6001 Perkins Road in
Oxnard, California. The WRRF is a conventional secondary treatment, activated-sludge facility with a design capacity of
31.7 million gallons per day. The liquid-stream processes include screening, grit removal and pumping, primary
clarification, interstage pumping, trickling filters, activated sludge treatment, secondary settling, flow equalization,
disinfection, and effluent pumping.
In addition to the liquid-stream treatment processes, the WRRF incorporates anaerobic digestion and a cogeneration
system that utilizes digester biogas to produce electricity and provide heat for the digestion process. Anaerobically
digested biosolids are dewatered using belt filter presses and transported offsite to a composting facility by a third party.
The cogeneration facility, constructed in 1975, operates using three engine-driven generators. These aging units have
become increasingly unreliable, and Generator No. 3 experienced a failure beyond repair and was permanently taken
offline in the summer of 2024. The remaining two cogeneration units are critical for the continued operation of the
Wastewater Facility as they are currently the sole source of heat for the digestion process. Most recently, Engine #2 was
taken out of service for maintenance. The work has been completed and the unit is back in service. Cogenerator #1
requires complex maintenance and is currently out of service. Having only one cogeneration unit in service puts the
digestion process at great risk of violating our National Pollution Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit. Permit
violation can result in significant fines.
DISCUSSION
On June 2, 2025, the Purchasing Division released Request for Bid (RFB) 25-136 for On-Call Maintenance and Repair
Services of Cogenerators and Plant Power Backup Generators for the Wastewater Division (Generator Maintenance
Services), with a bid due date of July 10, 2025. RFB 25-136 was directly sent to 3 service providers and published on the
City’s website, as well as www.publicpurchase.com. Following the closure of RFB 25-136, the City received a sole
response from Collicutt. After review by the Purchasing Division, Collicutt's bid was deemed responsive and an award
was issued. Collicutt has been in business for over 32 years and its specialized technical expertise has consistently
resulted in satisfactory generator maintenance services for the Wastewater Division and the continued operation of the
cogeneration facility. Additionally, the Wastewater Division does not always have the in-house capability to perform the
required maintenance activities of the generators and engines. Maintaining a reliable service provider for these services
ensures equipment remains operational and reduces the risk of downtime or permit violations.
On August 1, 2025, the Purchasing Agent executed Agreement 32600082 with Collicutt for the services provided in RFB
25-136. Following the catastrophic failure of Generator No. 3, the WRRF has had to rely on Cogenerator units No. 1 and
No. 2 for heat and electricity. Both units are aging and increasingly unreliable. The condition of the units has resulted in
more frequent breakdowns and a greater need for maintenance and repair work by Collicutt, which is within their area of
expertise and can be performed. An amendment to the agreement is requested to allow for the increased service needs
through the total agreement term ending July 31, 2028, if extended.
STRATEGIC PRIORITIES
This agenda item supports the Infrastructure and Natural Resources strategy. The purpose of the Infrastructure and
Natural Resources strategy is to preserve and improve our roads, utilities, parks, trees, water supply, and natural resources
through effective planning, prioritization, and an equitable and efficient use of available funding.
FINANCIAL IMPACT
The total amount of this First Amendment to Agreement 32600082 with Collicutt shall not exceed $495,000 for generator
maintenance services, through the originally authorized contract term of July 31, 2028, if extended. Funding for this
agreement shall be on an on-call basis with no guarantee of utilizing the full contract capacity since work is as-needed,
with staff approval. Funding shall come from the Wastewater Fund (611) account 6113614-53200 and sufficient budget
exists in the City Council-approved FY 2025/26 Operating Budget.
COMMITTEE OUTCOME
This item did not originate in Committee per the City Council Committee Bylaws Resolution 15,851, Article II, Section
D.3.h as this is a routine and recurring maintenance item necessary to keep public facilities operable that has a financial
impact under $500,000.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA REPORT
INFORMATION/CONSENT AGENDA
AGENDA ITEM NO. L.13
DATE: December 16, 2025
TO: City Council
FROM: Michael Wolfe, Public Works Director, (805) 385-8055, michael.wolfe@oxnard.org
SUBJECT: Agreement 32600227 with Northern Digital, Inc. for Water System Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) Improvements Project.
RECOMMENDATION
That the City Council approve and authorize the Mayor to execute an Agreement with Northern Digital, Inc. (NDI) for an
initial term of one year from December 17, 2025, to December 16, 2026, with an option for a one-year extension ending
December 16, 2027 for a total amount not to exceed $237,348.00 for the Water System Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) Improvements Project.
(This item did not originate in Committee as this is a capital improvement project specifically listed in the City's Capital
Improvement Program budget, which was previously approved by the City Council.)
BACKGROUND
On July 2, 2024, City Council approved and authorized the Mayor to execute Agreement 32500032 with Innovative
Engineering Systems, Inc. (Agilitech) in the not-to-exceed amount of $686,658 for Construction Services related to the
Water System SCADA Improvement Project (C2026). The project scope includes procurement and installation or
equipment and software for a new SCADA system at the Water Division. Programming and integration were purposely
not included in the scope of work due to system security and limiting access to the system from entities outside of the
City. As such, there is a need for a system programmer for integration. There is a current on-call agreement (Agreement
32400003) with NDI for Water and Water and Wastewater On-call SCADA Services. However, the on-call agreement
will not be used. The purpose of establishing a standalone contract is to establish these services for a specific capital
improvement program (CIP) project and align these required services to comply with the newly established purchasing
ordinance. This approach improves expenditure tracking and supports the Department’s goal of streamlining contract
administration for large capital projects.
As the selected system programmer and integrator, and to ensure continuity, maintain efficiency, security, and better align
with the specific needs of this project, the Water Division is now requesting to establish a standalone contract with NDI to
complete programming, commissioning, and start-up of the new SCADA system, as it relates to the Water System
SCADA Improvement Project. The Capital Improvement Program project is currently 25% complete and remains in
active construction.
Capital Improvement Program (CIP) Reference:
Project No. C2026 - Water System SCADA Improvements - CIP 2025-2029 - Adopted June 4, 2024 - Page 167.
DISCUSSION
A negotiated sole source contract is requested as NDI is the most reasonable source for this work due to their extensive
involvement with the City’s facilities, programming and control logic, ongoing coordination with the construction
contractor, and professional liability as the City’s on-call integrator. Their continued involvement is essential for
providing timely responses to requests for information, reviewing submittals, issuing design clarifications, and evaluating
potential field changes. The standalone NSS contract ensures adherence to the new purchasing Ordinance 3053 passed by
City Council on April 15, 2025, specifically Section 4-9, which states:
4-9 ON-CALL AGREEMENTS
(G) Task Orders issued for professional services subject to Article III and related to a Capital Improvement Project
shall not exceed $220,000.
Given that NDI requires additional funding through the end of Project C2026, a standalone contract is recommended to be
established as task orders may not be issued in excess of $220,000 for capital improvement projects under the new
Purchasing Ordinance.
STRATEGIC PRIORITIES
This agenda item supports the Infrastructure and Natural Resources strategy. The purpose of the Infrastructure and
Natural Resources strategy is to preserve and improve our roads, utilities, parks, trees, water supply, and natural resources
through effective planning, prioritization, and an equitable and efficient use of available funding.
FINANCIAL IMPACT
The total cost for this Agreement with NDI shall not exceed $237,348 through the contract term ending December 16,
2027 and funded from the Water System Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Improvements Project
(C2026). There is currently $591,839 available in the Water Capital Fund (602), funded from the Water Operating Fund
(601), to fund this agreement.
COMMITTEE OUTCOME
This item did not originate in Committee as this is a capital improvement project specifically listed in the City's Capital
Improvement Program budget, which was previously approved by the City Council.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA REPORT
INFORMATION/CONSENT AGENDA
AGENDA ITEM NO. L.6
DATE: October 29, 2024
TO: City Council
FROM: Michael Wolfe, Public Works Director, (805) 385-8055, michael.wolfe@oxnard.org
SUBJECT: Annual Purchase Orders with Badger Meters, Inc. for Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) Capable
Water Meters.
RECOMMENDATION
That the City Council approve and authorize the Purchasing Agent to execute annual purchase orders with Badger Meter,
Inc. for a total amount not to exceed value of $975,000 through June 30, 2029, for the supply of Advanced Metering
Infrastructure (AMI) Capable Water Meters.
(Public Works and Transportation Committee approved 3-0 on October 8, 2024.)
BACKGROUND
The City of Oxnard’s Water Division is responsible for the transmission and distribution of potable water to City
customers. The Water Division delivers over 20 million gallons per day of safe and reliable potable and recycled water
supply to customers. The City water system includes: 10 water wells, five turnouts from the United Water Conservation
District’s Oxnard-Hueneme Pipeline system, one turnout from the Calleguas Municipal Water District’s water system,
one groundwater desalter facility, six blending stations, and over 500 miles of transmission and distribution pipelines and
over 43,000 existing water meters.
On October 19, 2021, Capital Improvement Project No. 206503 – Advanced Meter Infrastructure (AMI) Replacement
Project was approved by the City Council. At the time of this staff report, the AMI Replacement Project is 85% complete.
The project scope of work includes the replacement of all existing water meters in the City’s water distribution system
and does not include meters for new development. The intent of this purchase order is to procure meters associated with
new development and auxiliary dwelling units (ADU).
DISCUSSION
A negotiated single-source purchase order is necessary with Badger Meters, Inc to ensure future compatibility when the
AMI meters are installed. The AMI capital improvement project agreement and its authority does not include the ability
for the Water Division to directly order water meters. To maintain future compatibility and minimize wasted resources,

FROM: Michael Wolfe, Public Works Director, (805) 385-8055, michael.wolfe@oxnard.org
SUBJECT: Public Project Agreement 32400281 with Quinn Company dba. Quinn Power Systems for On-Call
Stationary Generators Maintenance and Minor Repair Services (Rebid), Specification No. PW 24-15R.
RECOMMENDATION
That the City Council approve and authorize the Mayor to Execute an Agreement with Quinn Company dba Quinn Power
Systems (Quinn) in the amount not to exceed $420,000 for a three-year term ending from the effective date of the
agreement for on-call stationary generators maintenance and minor repair services.
(Public Works and Transportation Committee approved 3-0 on January 23, 2024.)
BACKGROUND
The City of Oxnard has multiple divisions that utilize stationary generators, including water, wastewater, fire, and police,
all requiring scheduled and non-scheduled or unplanned repair and maintenance from time to time. In order to avoid
regulatory non-compliance, public health and safety hazards, property and/or environmental damage, the work must be
completed with urgency, requiring a quick response from a contractor. To respond promptly to these planned and
unplanned infrastructure repairs, the City requires an on-call contract with a qualified contractor that has diverse technical
capabilities as well as the ability to respond quickly to the City’s needs.
The City has maintained similar contracts for many years to streamline the contracting process, allowing for regular
maintenance, scheduled repairs and quick response to unplanned and urgent repair needs.
Services to be completed by the Contractor are categorized as follows:
Non-Scheduled Maintenance, Services and Repairs
The Contractor will provide on-call non-scheduled urgent service twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per
week. The Contractor must verbally respond within two (2) hours of telephone or email notification by the City. The
Contractor must be on the site within four (4) hours of the notification and begin work immediately. Work may include
after-hours, weekends and/or holidays.
Urgent repairs are those where public interest and necessity demand an immediate response to avoid harm to, or to
safeguard life, health or property.
When the extent of urgency is no longer necessary because the threat to public health and safety and/or property is no
longer present, the Contractor shall coordinate with the Project Manager or designee to schedule minor repair and
maintenance work.
Scheduled Quarterly Inspections, Annual Inspections, Load Bank Testing, and Minor Repair Work
The Contractor must verbally respond within twenty-four (24) hours of telephone or email notification by the City. The
scope of work and schedule shall be mutually agreed to between City staff and the Contractor before Work begins. Work
under this category shall be planned and scheduled Monday through Friday during normal City business hours unless
otherwise agreed to by the City.
The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary labor, materials, equipment and other incidental and appurtenant
work to provide on-call stationary generator maintenance and minor repair services for multiple divisions and facilities
throughout the City. This agreement will be a task order-based, time and material contract. The Contractor shall provide
a written estimate of services before a task order is issued.
DISCUSSION
The specific Work for these services includes providing on-call stationary generator maintenance and minor repair
services for the twenty-seven (27) City-owned generators located at various locations throughout the City. Annually,
these generators require Preventative Maintenance Checks and Services (PMCS), Load Bank Testing, unscheduled
services and/or minor repairs to maintain regular operations, and all other appurtenant and associated work in accordance
with the Contract Documents.
There were two (2) public bid attempts made by procurement staff that resulted in zero responsive bids. The first notice
inviting formal bids (NIFB) on the Project was published on September 7, 2023, and all bids were due on October 5,
2023. The second NIFB was published on October 12, 2023, and all bids were due and opened on November 2, 2023.
The City received zero responsive bids. Following City purchasing policies for requirements to secure a Sole Source
Agreement, City staff obtained pricing from Quinn. Procurement staff reviewed all documentation received from Quinn
and its subcontractors, verified possession of required currently valid licenses, reviewed the federal Occupational Safety
and Health Administration (OSHA) website for safety violations, and verified registration with the California Department
of Industrial Relations (DIR). Based upon the available information and research performed to date, staff believes that the
Contractor is capable of satisfactorily completing the services. Thus, staff recommends that the City Council award the
Agreement for these services to Quinn.

March 16, 2021.

INFORMATION/CONSENT AGENDA

TO: City Council
FROM: Michael Wolfe, Public Works Director, (805) 385-8055, michael.wolfe@oxnard.org
SUBJECT: Agreement 32400297 with Petroleum Telcom, Inc. dba Telcom, Inc. for Mobile Radio Equipment, Parts
and Accessories; and Installation, Repair and Maintenance Services.
RECOMMENDATION
That the City Council approve and authorize an Agreement with Petroleum Telcom, Inc. dba Telcom, Inc. for a one-year
term with the option to extend for four consecutive one-year periods for a maximum contract term of five years, and a
total contract not-to-exceed amount over the entire possible contract term of $900,000 for Mobile Radio Equipment, Parts
and Accessories; and Installation, Repair and Maintenance Services on an on-call/as-needed basis.
(Public Works and Transportation Committee approved 3-0 on January 23, 2024.)
BACKGROUND
The City’s fleet is standardized with Motorola and JVC Kenwood two-way radios. The City’s Fire and Police
Departments purchase Motorola and Kenwood radios for their emergency response vehicles and equipment. In addition,
the Fleet Services Division of the Public Works Department is responsible for performing maintenance and repairs on the
City fleet. These services include equipment such as two-way radios, antennas and associated equipment that is installed
on Public Works and emergency response vehicles. Due to workload and technical expertise, the Fleet Division
recommends the use of a vendor to purchase, install and provide maintenance and repair services on an on-call/as-needed
basis.
Petroleum Telcom, Inc. dba Telcom, Inc., is headquartered in Oxnard. They specialize in two-way radios, data and
communications as well as other services that include sales, installation and services. Telcom, Inc. is an authorized
Kenwood Communications Division dealer for parts, service and support and is also a channel-level partner for Motorola
Solutions for the regional area of California, Arizona, and Nevada through its primary office in Oxnard. Fleet Services
has been using Telcom, Inc. for over 20 years. All new equipment, installations, services, repairs and warranties are
performed by authorized dealers and/or partners; therefore, it is necessary to obtain these services and OEM parts from
Telcom, Inc.
DISCUSSION
Telcom is the only Kenwood and Motorola authorized dealer for support and service in the area. City Purchasing Policy
allows for the City to enter into agreements with vendors without competitive bidding when there is only a single source
available to provide the required products and/or services. Having access to the authorized dealer with access to
equipment, parts and services ensures maintenance can be performed in an efficient manner and warranty services can be
obtained.
The City's Police and Fire Departments operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, providing a full range of emergency
and non-emergency services to the community. They must be able to communicate in any situation via two-way radios
installed in their vehicles. The Fleet Services Division is responsible for keeping these radios operational and in working
order. As these radios are installed in critical emergency vehicles, it is imperative to maintain them with minimal
downtime. In order to achieve this, Fleet Services at times will require these services and repairs to be performed by
Telcom, Inc. under the direction of Fleet Services.
Telcom, Inc. is located in Oxnard and meets all required City contractual provisions, including possession of a City
business tax certificate, insurance certificates and corporate filing with the California Secretary of State. Based upon the
available information and research performed to date, staff believes the vendor is capable of satisfactorily completing the
services in this Agreement. Thus, staff recommends that the City Council award this Agreement to Petroleum Telcom,
Inc. dba Telcom, Inc.
STRATEGIC PRIORITIES
This agenda item is a routine operational item or does not relate to the five strategic priorities adopted by City Council on
March 16, 2021.
FINANCIAL IMPACT
The total cost for this agreement with Petroleum Telcom, Inc. dba Telcom, Inc. shall not exceed $900,000 through
February 20, 2029, if extended all years. Funding will begin in Fiscal Year 2023-24 and there is sufficient funding for all
departments/divisions in the City Council approved FY 2023-24 Operating Budget. Subsequent fiscal year funding will
be requested in the annual budget process.

PUBLIC WORKS AND TRANSPORTATION COMMITTEE
AGENDA REPORT
REPORTS
AGENDA ITEM NO. D.1
DATE: January 23, 2024
TO: Public Works and Transportation Committee
FROM: Michael Wolfe, Public Works Director, (805) 385-8055, michael.wolfe@oxnard.org
SUBJECT: Public Project Agreement 32400281 with Quinn Company dba. Quinn Power Systems for On-
Call Stationary Generators Maintenance and Minor Repair Services (Rebid), Specification No.
PW 24-15R. (10 minutes)
RECOMMENDATION
That the Public Works and Transportation Committee recommend that the City Council approve and authorize
the Mayor to Execute an Agreement with Quinn Company dba Quinn Power Systems (Quinn) in the amount
not to exceed $420,000 for a three-year term ending from the effective date of the agreement for on-call
stationary generators maintenance and minor repair services.
Please click the following link to view the required Measure M pre-recorded presentation
video: https://youtu.be/qyJiYQLeenA
BACKGROUND
The City of Oxnard has multiple divisions that utilize stationary generators, including water, wastewater, fire,
and police, all requiring scheduled and non-scheduled or unplanned repair and maintenance from time to time.
In order to avoid regulatory non-compliance, public health and safety hazards, property and/or environmental
damage, the work must be completed with urgency, requiring a quick response from a contractor. To respond
promptly to these planned and unplanned infrastructure repairs, the City requires an on-call contract with a
qualified contractor that has diverse technical capabilities as well as the ability to respond quickly to the City’s
needs.
The City has maintained similar contracts for many years to streamline the contracting process, allowing for
regular maintenance, scheduled repairs and quick response to unplanned and urgent repair needs.
Services to be completed by the Contractor are categorized as follows:
Non-Scheduled Maintenance, Services and Repairs
The Contractor will provide on-call non-scheduled urgent service twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7)
days per week. The Contractor must verbally respond within two (2) hours of telephone or email notification by
the City. The Contractor must be on the site within four (4) hours of the notification and begin work
immediately. Work may include after-hours, weekends and/or holidays.
Urgent repairs are those where public interest and necessity demand an immediate response to avoid harm to, or
to safeguard life, health or property.
When the extent of urgency is no longer necessary because the threat to public health and safety and/or
property is no longer present, the Contractor shall coordinate with the Project Manager or designee to schedule
minor repair and maintenance work.
Scheduled Quarterly Inspections, Annual Inspections, Load Bank Testing, and Minor Repair Work
The Contractor must verbally respond within twenty-four (24) hours of telephone or email notification by the
City. The scope of work and schedule shall be mutually agreed to between City staff and the Contractor before
Work begins. Work under this category shall be planned and scheduled Monday through Friday during normal
City business hours unless otherwise agreed to by the City.
The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary labor, materials, equipment and other incidental and
appurtenant work to provide on-call stationary generator maintenance and minor repair services for multiple
divisions and facilities throughout the City. This agreement will be a task order-based, time and material
contract. The Contractor shall provide a written estimate of services before a task order is issued.
DISCUSSION
The specific Work for these services includes providing on-call stationary generator maintenance and minor
repair services for the twenty-seven (27) City-owned generators located at various locations throughout the
City. Annually, these generators require Preventative Maintenance Checks and Services (PMCS), Load Bank
Testing, unscheduled services and/or minor repairs to maintain regular operations, and all other appurtenant and
associated work in accordance with the Contract Documents.
There were two (2) public bid attempts made by procurement staff that resulted in zero responsive bids. The
first notice inviting formal bids (NIFB) on the Project was published on September 7, 2023, and all bids were
due on October 5, 2023. The second NIFB was published on October 12, 2023, and all bids were due and
opened on November 2, 2023. The City received zero responsive bids. Following City purchasing policies for
requirements to secure a Sole Source Agreement, City staff obtained pricing from Quinn. Procurement staff
reviewed all documentation received from Quinn and its subcontractors, verified possession of required
currently valid licenses, reviewed the federal Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) website
for safety violations, and verified registration with the California Department of Industrial Relations (DIR).
Based upon the available information and research performed to date, staff believes that the Contractor is
capable of satisfactorily completing the services. Thus, staff recommends that the City Council award the
Agreement for these services to Quinn.
STRATEGIC PRIORITIES
This agenda item is a routine operational item or does not relate to the five strategic priorities adopted by City
Council on March 16, 2021.
FINANCIAL IMPACT
The total cost for this Agreement with Quinn shall not exceed $420,000 over the three (3) year term of this
Agreement. Funding shall be provided by the Water Fund (601), Wastewater Fund (611) and the Fleet Services
Fund (741). Each service provided through this Agreement shall be issued by a task order and subject to
available funding. Staff within each Division will ensure sufficient funding of tasks prior to initiating task
orders or incurring services, consistent with the City Council approved Operating Budgets. Subsequent fiscal
year funding will be requested in the annual budget process.

RECOMMENDATION
That the Public Works and Transportation Committee recommend that the City Council approve and authorize
an Agreement with Petroleum Telcom, Inc. dba Telcom, Inc. for a one-year term with the option to extend for
four consecutive one-year periods for a maximum contract term of five years, and a total contract not-to-exceed
amount over the entire possible contract term of $900,000 for Mobile Radio Equipment, Parts and Accessories;
and Installation, Repair and Maintenance Services on an on-call/as-needed basis.

BACKGROUND
The City’s fleet is standardized with Motorola and JVC Kenwood two-way radios. The City’s Fire and Police
Departments purchase Motorola and Kenwood radios for their emergency response vehicles and equipment. In
addition, the Fleet Services Division of the Public Works Department is responsible for performing
maintenance and repairs on the City fleet. These services include equipment such as two-way radios, antennas
and associated equipment that is installed on Public Works and emergency response vehicles. Due to workload
and technical expertise, the Fleet Division recommends the use of a vendor to purchase, install and provide
maintenance and repair services on an on-call/as-needed basis.
Petroleum Telcom, Inc. dba Telcom, Inc., is headquartered in Oxnard. They specialize in two-way radios, data
and communications as well as other services that include sales, installation and services. Telcom, Inc. is an
authorized Kenwood Communications Division dealer for parts, service and support and is also a channel-level
partner for Motorola Solutions for the regional area of California, Arizona, and Nevada through its primary
office in Oxnard. Fleet Services has been using Telcom, Inc. for over 20 years. All new equipment,
installations, services, repairs and warranties are performed by authorized dealers and/or partners; therefore, it
is necessary to obtain these services and OEM parts from Telcom, Inc.
DISCUSSION
Telcom is the only Kenwood and Motorola authorized dealer for support and service in the area. City
Purchasing Policy allows for the City to enter into agreements with vendors without competitive bidding when
there is only a single source available to provide the required products and/or services. Having access to the
authorized dealer with access to equipment, parts and services ensures maintenance can be performed in an
efficient manner and warranty services can be obtained.
The City's Police and Fire Departments operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, providing a full range of
emergency and non-emergency services to the community. They must be able to communicate in any situation
via two-way radios installed in their vehicles. The Fleet Services Division is responsible for keeping these
radios operational and in working order. As these radios are installed in critical emergency vehicles, it is
imperative to maintain them with minimal downtime. In order to achieve this, Fleet Services at times will
require these services and repairs to be performed by Telcom, Inc. under the direction of Fleet Services.
Telcom, Inc. is located in Oxnard and meets all required City contractual provisions, including possession of a
City business tax certificate, insurance certificates and corporate filing with the California Secretary of State.
Based upon the available information and research performed to date, staff believes the vendor is capable of
satisfactorily completing the services in this Agreement. Thus, staff recommends that the City Council award
this Agreement to Petroleum Telcom, Inc. dba Telcom, Inc.

FINANCIAL IMPACT
The total cost for this agreement with Petroleum Telcom, Inc. dba Telcom, Inc. shall not exceed $900,000
through February 20, 2029, if extended all years. Funding will begin in Fiscal Year 2023-24 and there is

Subsequent fiscal year funding will be requested in the annual budget process.
